draft.subject: Lining up your bonds with the income you will draw
draft.english:
Dear [[FIRST_NAME]],

As you get closer to replacing your salary with income from the portfolio, I would like to look at when your bonds actually repay.

The plan we work to runs until 2036. Today 21.0% of your wealth is in bonds and similar holdings that do not repay until after that date, and together they are about USD 0.9m below what was paid for them. The largest is the US Treasury 3.875% due 2049. These are only certain to repay in full when they mature, which is after the period the income is meant to cover.

What I would suggest is that we line up the maturities with the income you will start drawing, moving gradually toward holdings that come due when you need them. It does not need to happen all at once, and we can keep the reserve in US dollars you wanted.

Could I call you this week to go through it?
